cover.artAlt: A Tyrannosaurus rex standing in a misty prehistoric forest at sunrise
cover.blurb: They ruled the Earth for over 160 million years. Turn the page and go back in time.

pages.title: Three Horns and a Giant Shield
pages.artAlt: A herd of Triceratops grazing on ferns in an open prehistoric plain

facts.text: Triceratops means three-horned face. Two long horns grew above its eyes and a shorter one sat on its nose, above a wide bony frill that spread out behind its head.
facts.source: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History (naturalhistory.si.edu)

facts.text: Its skull was one of the biggest heads any land animal has ever had, longer than a grown-up is tall.
Triceratops ate only plants. It had hundreds of teeth stacked in tight bundles that worked like scissors, slicing through tough ferns and branches.

pages.title: The Long-Necked Giants
pages.artAlt: Long-necked Brachiosaurus wading in a calm lake at sunset, reaching into tall trees

facts.text: Brachiosaurus had front legs that were longer than its back legs, so its whole body sloped upward and its head was carried very high, like a living crane.
The long-necked dinosaurs did not chew. They raked leaves off branches with peg-shaped teeth and swallowed them whole, letting their enormous stomachs do the rest of the work.
These giants, called sauropods, were the largest animals that ever walked on land. Some of them were heavier than ten elephants put together.

pages.title: Some Dinosaurs Had Feathers
pages.artAlt: A feathered Velociraptor standing alert in tall grass

facts.text: The real Velociraptor was about the size of a turkey, not the tall movie monster. Most of its length was a long, stiff tail it used for balance.
Fossil arm bones from Velociraptor have small bumps on them called quill knobs. On birds today, those same bumps are where feathers attach, so we know this dinosaur had feathers.
Birds are dinosaurs. Every sparrow and pigeon you see is descended from small feathered dinosaurs, which means one branch of the dinosaur family never went extinct.

pages.title: How We Know Any of This
pages.artAlt: A dinosaur skeleton half-uncovered at a fossil dig site in orange desert rock

facts.text: A fossil is not the original bone. When a dinosaur was buried quickly by mud or sand, minerals seeped in over millions of years and slowly turned the bone to stone.
Fossil hunters dig with brushes, dental picks and small hand tools, because a hammer would smash the very thing they came to find. Big bones get wrapped in a plaster jacket for the trip home.
Dinosaurs lived for over 160 million years. The last of them, apart from birds, died out about 66 million years ago after an enormous asteroid struck the Earth.
